newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: MALBAK TO PAY 350 MLN RAND NOW, MORE LATER.
newsitem.headline: MALBAK TO PAY 350 MLN RAND NOW, MORE LATER.

text.p: South Africa's Malbak Ltd will pay around 350 million rand in cash to shareholders on April 29 as part of its unbundling, to be topped up by a further distribution later, acting chief executive Peter Beningfield said on Tuesday.
"It is about a rand a share which will be paid out at this stage," Beningfield told Reuters.

"What the board has said is that they are cognisant of the need to pay the shareholders cash and they will look at a further distribution...once the remaining assets are sold and the liabilities are fully settled."

The unbundling of the diversified industrial holding group, was formally approved on Monday by shareholders. The plan has seen a raft of mostly unlisted investments sold off in recent months and plans laid to distribute shares in the listed companies.

Beningfield said the only assets still to be sold off are computer firm ICL and engineering company Osborn MMD. It was "highly unlikely" that they would be disposed of by the April deadline, hence the staggered payments to shareholders, he said.
"We are talking (to potential buyers), it will hopefully take between four and six weeks," Beningfield said.
The unbundling, set in motion last year to unlock the value of Malbak's underlying assets, follows similar actions by other major South African groups including Gencor Ltd and Barlow Ltd .
Malbak said last year that the cash raised from unpacking its units would exceed 700 million rand, but Beningfield said on Tuesday the composition of this amount had changed over time.

"When we calculated the 700 million, it assumed sales, for example, of MY. What has happened is that the entire make-up of the 700 million has changed, so what will be distributed on the April 29 is somewhere in the region of 350 million with the rest coming later."
He added, however, that the total value of the package to shareholders would be "very similar" to that originally announced.
The unbundling of Malbak's 64 percent stake in U.K-based MY Holdings Plc has been blocked by current South African exchange control regulations.
Malbak will therefore retain its interest in MY, alongside a stake in Kohler Ltd , leaving it as the holding company of two packaging groups.
Asked if either Kohler or MY would be delisted, Beningfield, who relinquishes his position on the board next month, said: "That is a question for the new board."
Beningfield, who also heads up subsidiary South African Druggists Ltd (SAD), said the unbundling exercise had been more complex than originally envisaged.
"(But) it has actually gone quite smoothly although it hasn't been easy. I am delighted we have got through it in what has effectively been six to seven months," he said.

Assets sold off include freight company Eagle Freight, steel firm Stalcor, electrical business Tedelex, appliance group Defy and automotive group Malbak Motor Holdings sold off. A stake in engineering group Haggie Ltd was also sold, with the remaining 20 percent stake to be distributed.
Shares in the other listed companies, including Ellerine Holdings Ltd , Foodcorp Ltd , New Clicks Holdings and SAD, will also be dispersed.
